findings.issue: No tests, no test runner, no test script anywhere in app/ despite ~750 LOC of non-trivial logic
findings.suggestion: Add a lightweight runner (node --test needs zero deps) with unit tests for lib/format.mjs and lib/api.mjs helpers, plus a few route-level tests via app.fetch() against a stubbed API

findings.issue: sortRows encodes subtle semantics — missing values forced to the end regardless of direction, numeric vs string comparison per column, moveName tie-break — with nothing pinning them down
findings.suggestion: Unit-test sortRows directly (it's a pure function): ascending/descending per column, em-dash/null placement, tie-breaks, and level-0 rows

findings.issue: getPokemonMoveInfo is the most complex pipeline in the app (version-group ordering, latest-game default, per-method dedup) and is only exercised end-to-end by acceptance tests against real data
findings.suggestion: Extract and test with fixture payloads: unknown requestedGame falls back to the highest-order group, rows deduped by method+move, method ordering via compareMethods

findings.issue: The in-memory promise cache is global, unbounded (every pokemon, move, and version-group response cached forever) and offers no injection point, which also makes future tests order-dependent
findings.suggestion: Add a TTL or LRU bound and expose a clear/flush hook (or make the cache injectable) and test the rejection-deletes-key behaviour

findings.issue: Pagination clamping and page normalisation (?page=abc → 1, ?page=999 → last page, slice bounds) are untested edge behaviour
findings.suggestion: Unit-test normalizePage and the clamping arithmetic, including the empty-result case where the pagination block is omitted

findings.issue: buildQuery is the URL-state contract (param order, dropping page=1, preserving q/type/generation in pagination links and HX-Push-Url) with no test
findings.suggestion: Unit-test buildQuery for all filter combinations and the page-omission rule; it is the regression point for shareable URLs

findings.issue: Partial-render branches keyed on the HX-Request header (moves section vs full page, moves-table swap target) have no route-level tests; a changed hx-target or swap mode breaks them silently in a way unit tests of pure functions won't catch
findings.suggestion: Add app.fetch()-based tests asserting the htmx branch returns only the #moves section plus the HX-Push-Url header, and the moves-table route returns exactly one <table>

findings.issue: Spec-critical pure helpers (latestEnglishFlavorText must take the LAST English entry and collapse whitespace; humanize capitalisation; dexNumber zero-padding) are untested one-liners that a refactor could silently flip (e.g. .find vs .at(-1))
findings.suggestion: Cover format.mjs with table-driven unit tests; zero cost, high regression value

findings.issue: Error handling is untested: only API 404s map to the styled not-found page; any other API failure falls through to app.onError's plain-text 500
findings.suggestion: Test NotFoundError → 404 HTML per route, and that a simulated API 500 yields the 500 text response rather than a crash

findings.issue: englishName duplicates format.mjs's englishOrHumanized lookup logic; with no tests, the two can drift apart unnoticed
findings.suggestion: Delete the duplicate and use englishOrHumanized (or test both)

summary: The agent wrote zero tests of its own — no runner, no script, nothing — leaving ~750 lines of genuinely risky logic (multi-key sorting with missing-value rules, filtering, pagination clamping, URL-state construction, a global promise cache) guarded only by the borrowed acceptance suite. Most of the riskiest code is pure or nearly pure functions that would have been cheap to test with node --test and no new dependencies. Once anyone refactors the data layer or the move-table pipeline, regressions in sort ordering, URL shape, or cache behaviour will ship silently.
